question_text: Find the derivative of tan⁻¹(√((1 − cos x)/(1 + cos x))).

mark_split.label: Replace 1 − cos x and 1 + cos x by half-angle forms
Cancel the inverse tangent and differentiate x/2

steps.label: Replace 1 − cos x and 1 + cos x by half-angle forms
steps.margin_note: First mark, and the step the rest of the answer depends on. The two half-angle identities 1 − cos x = 2sin²(x/2) and 1 + cos x = 2cos²(x/2) turn the fraction under the root into a perfect square, so the square root is removed.
steps.memory_tip: Whenever 1 − cos x and 1 + cos x appear together under a root, write both in half-angle form: the 2s cancel and a square is left.

recall.must_convey: That 1 − cos x = 2sin²(x/2) and 1 + cos x = 2cos²(x/2), so the radicand is tan²(x/2).

steps.why: Differentiating the printed expression by the chain and quotient rules is long and rarely finishes correctly. The half-angle identities remove the root and the fraction in one line, which is what the first mark is for.
common_mistakes: Using 1 − cos x = 2cos²(x/2), swapping the sine and cosine forms.
Writing √(tan²(x/2)) as tan(x/2) with no statement of the range, when the square root is |tan(x/2)|.

steps.label: Cancel the inverse tangent and differentiate x/2
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Tan⁻¹(tan θ) = θ only when θ is inside (−π/2, π/2), and x/2 is, so y is simply x/2. The derivative of x/2 is the constant 1/2.
steps.memory_tip: For 0 < x < π the expression reduces to x/2, so the derivative is a constant and no chain rule is needed.

steps.why: This mark is for recognising that the answer is a constant. A student who keeps differentiating the original fraction will produce something that only reduces to 1/2 after several more lines.
common_mistakes: Writing the inner derivative of tan(x/2) as ½ instead of ½sec²(x/2), which gives 1/(2(1 + tan²(x/2))) instead of 1/2.
Giving the answer as x/2, which is y and not dy/dx.

insider_note: The half-angle identities turn the fraction into tan²(x/2), so for 0 < x < π the root and the Tan⁻¹ cancel and y is just x/2. The answer there is the constant 1/2.
